title: Thyroxine in goiter, Helicobacter pylori infection, and chronic gastritis
authors: Centanni M, Gargano L, Canettieri G, Viceconti N, Franchi A, Delle Fave G, et al.
population: Patients with euthyroid multinodular goitre given thyroxine to a TSH of 0.05 to 0.20 mU/l: 135 without gastric disorders, 53 with H. pylori gastritis, 60 with atrophic body gastritis; prospective series of 11 patients before and after H. pylori infection and 10 patients before and during omeprazole
funder: Supported by a grant (G 107919) from La Sapienza University, Rome.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.
result: The reference group needed a median of 100 µg/day (1.53 µg/kg/day); the daily requirement was 22% to 34% higher with H. pylori gastritis, atrophic gastritis or both. In 11 patients, new H. pylori infection raised median TSH from 0.11 to 1.35 mU/l at an unchanged dose; after eradication, TSH 0.12 mU/l was regained at a median of 1.70 against 1.56 µg/kg/day. In 10 patients, omeprazole 40 mg/day raised median TSH to 1.70 mU/l, and a 37% higher median dose (2.16 against 1.58 µg/kg/day) was needed to regain suppression.
